issue.title: Offline Codex preflight can accept an effort that ordinary startup rejects
issue.body:
Origin: the independent Claude Opus 5.5 xhigh review of #448, [original review](https://github.com/Jacob-J-Thomas/GraphGoblin/issues/448#issuecomment-7060237320). This is a pre-existing P3 follow-up, outside #448's bounded missing-seed projection. Source is signed main `02351e2fb932b3be44e7cc3fb3943a61d568226c`; the reviewed candidate preserves this behavior. This record is not implementation or acceptance.

`apps/api/src/preflight.ts:265-289` checks only Codex model membership and enabled state. Ordinary startup also validates the selected effort through `validateHarnessDefaults`. For a configured `gpt-5.5` / `none`, offline preflight can report the default ready and exit 0, while startup rejects `EFFORT_UNSUPPORTED`. The maintained #448 regression at `apps/api/src/preflight-catalog.test.ts:203-211` records the existing disagreement rather than fixing it.

Acceptance when separately dispatched:
- Reproduce with disposable supported/current stores and the public offline command/startup; include supported-effort and missing-effort controls.
- Make the Codex default result truthfully account for the effective effort, with no model/provider turn or automatic substitution.
- Preserve read-only database/WAL behavior, stored enabled preferences, existing harness readiness separation and the documented SQLite SHM reader exception.
- Do not silently align Codex/Claude disabled-model severity or expand model retirement policy; select any such product change separately.
- Update preflight documentation and meaningful positive/negative tests; retain numerical coverage, independent QA, opposite-family review and current-target CI.

Duplicate check included open/closed preflight-title, preflight/effort, pending-migration and startup/seed searches; #448 covers missing seeds, #179 CLI prerequisite capability and #132 template-catalog repeated work. None owns this effort-check discrepancy. Delivery: parked backlog, no implementation gate; proposed Sol xhigh implementation and Opus xhigh review. Not added to the current 26-core-issue batch.

issue.title: Pending-migration preflight can disagree with startup's stored model catalog
issue.body:
Origin: the independent Claude Opus 5.5 xhigh review of #448, [original review](https://github.com/Jacob-J-Thomas/GraphGoblin/issues/448#issuecomment-7060237320). This is a pre-existing P3 follow-up, outside #448's bounded missing-seed projection. Source is signed main `02351e2fb932b3be44e7cc3fb3943a61d568226c`; the reviewed candidate preserves this behavior. This record is not implementation or acceptance.

When migrations are pending, `runPreflight` uses the shipped default catalog (`apps/api/src/preflight.ts:366`) instead of stored rows and describes it as the catalog seeded on first start. Ordinary startup can read a current-format store through `readPreMigrationModelCatalog` and admits from stored rows plus missing seeds before migrating. Offline and ordinary startup can therefore disagree about a stored model, disabled flag or supported effort on this path. This finding is source-backed; the review did not execute a new pending-migration reproduction.

Acceptance when separately dispatched:
- Independently reproduce a current-format/pending-migration store where stored metadata differs from shipped seeds; include a clean migrated store, missing store and unsupported/unreadable store.
- Define a truthful read-only pre-migration admission result consistent with the startup guard where safe. If a model projection cannot safely be inspected, distinguish that limit rather than asserting unsupported model or ready execution from unrelated seed data.
- Never migrate, seed, refresh, create or alter the inspected database/WAL; preserve the SQLite SHM reader exception and failure closure of unsupported formats.
- Keep stored owner disablement, provider/account readiness, and model-retirement policy separate; no automatic model substitution.
- Verify the public command/startup distinction and update documentation under normal review/QA/coverage/CI gates.

Duplicate check included open/closed preflight-title, pending-migration/catalog and startup/seed searches. #448 explicitly handles current migrated stores; #179 is CLI prerequisite capability, and #495 is aliased-checkout repository guards. This is a separate pre-existing path. Delivery: parked backlog, no implementation gate; proposed Sol xhigh implementation and Opus xhigh review. Not added to the current 26-core-issue batch.

comments.body:
Current source observation from [#448's independent review](https://github.com/Jacob-J-Thomas/GraphGoblin/issues/448#issuecomment-7060237320), preserved for this parked model-capability policy record and its consolidated #271 report:

On signed `02351e2fb932b3be44e7cc3fb3943a61d568226c`, startup admission checks stored harness-row efforts before `SqliteModelCatalog.seed()` refreshes harness-owned display/effort metadata. A newly added effort can require an initial start with a different default; a removed effort can pass the old admission and disappear during the subsequent seed refresh. These are source-derived transition cases, not newly executed owner observations. Existing enabled preferences remain preserved.

#448 deliberately keeps stored-first admission, and D172 does not change lifecycle or repair policy. Keep this transition question with the existing #262/#271 capability-policy context for future refinement; this comment does not add an accepted requirement, alter post-1.0 scope, unpark the issue, authorize rewriting stored content, or admit #262 to the current five-intent batch. A future decision should distinguish capability additions from removals and reconcile admission with the intended effective catalog while preserving pinned runs, explicit owner choices and no runtime model fallback.
